citations.narrative:
The outside area for the oriental clawed otter had a large pool with an area of round smooth rocks along one edge
separating the pool form the grassy / dirt area. There was an accumulation of a damp dark black-dark green material
between the rocks especially along the edge of the pool.
At the time of inspection, the keeper was performing a partial water change and refilling the pool. However, the water was
still moderately murky and green from the presence of algae. Some algae was also on the surface of the pool. Otters
spend significant time in the water demonstrating species typical behavior. The otter enclosure should be cleaned in a
manner that prevents buildup of dirt and organic material and that improves the clarity of the water from algae growth. The
buildup of organic matter shall be removed from primary enclosures as often as necessary to prevent contamination of the
animals and to minimize disease hazards. Correct by November 1, 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representative and licensee.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
